findings.source_quote: οὗ μὴ ἀφιστάμενός τις οὐκ ἔχει πλανηθῆναι
findings.english_quote: from which no one who refrains from departing can be led astray
findings.issue: In Greek, οὗ supplies the complement of ἀφιστάμενος: someone who does not depart from the rule cannot be led astray. In the English, “from which” attaches most naturally to “be led astray,” making the assurance sound limited to being diverted from the rule. The draft's lexical note explains the Greek correctly, but the main sentence does not clearly express that construction.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “Anyone who does not depart from it cannot be led astray.” Retain this after the statement about grasping the truth of the rule of pairing, and review the revised sentence afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἡ κακία πάλιν, ὡς αὐτὴ βασιλεύουσα
findings.english_quote: evil once again, as though it itself were reigning
findings.issue: “As though” suggests an apparent or hypothetical reign. The construction ὡς with the participle can instead present the grounds or role attributed to evil: “as itself holding sway.” The draft does not explain its selection of the apparent-role nuance or preserve the materially different explanatory reading. This is an undisclosed interpretive choice, not a source defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer the less prejudicial wording “evil once again, as itself holding sway.” Alternatively, retain “as though” only with a contextual explanation of the personifying comparison and a note preserving “as itself holding sway” or “since it itself held sway.” Any changed text or notes require fresh review.
